title: U.S. House · Indiana's 5th District
area: Central Indiana, including the northern Indianapolis suburbs (Hamilton, Madison, and surrounding counties)

context.text: Incumbent Victoria Spartz won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Scott King, 59.9% to 40.1%. J.D. Ford, an Indiana state senator, won a seven-candidate Democratic primary with 42.5% of the vote.

candidates.name: Victoria Spartz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Scott King, 59.9% to 40.1%

summary.text: Victoria Spartz is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 5th District, born in Ukraine and first elected to Congress in 2020 after serving in the Indiana Senate.

background.text: Born in Nosivka, Ukraine, in 1978. Earned a bachelor's and MBA from the National University of Economics in Kyiv and an M.P.A. from Indiana University in 2006.
Worked as a certified public accountant and auditor before entering politics.
Served in the Indiana Senate from 2017 to 2020.

Serves on the Joint Economic Committee in the 119th Congress; previously served on the House Judiciary Committee's Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust and Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement subcommittees.

record.text: Assigned to the Joint Economic Committee for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Judiciary Committee during the 118th Congress (2023-2024), including its Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust subcommittee.

candidates.name: J.D. Ford
candidates.ballotNote: Won a seven-candidate May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 42.5% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Indiana State Senator, District 29 (2018-2026; not seeking re-election to the state Senate)

summary.text: J.D. Ford is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 5th District. He has represented Indiana Senate District 29 since 2018, becoming the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly, and is not seeking re-election to the state Senate.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and criminal justice from the University of Akron and a master's degree in education from Purdue University.
Worked as senior director of recruitment and expansion for Theta Chi Fraternity, Inc.
Elected to Indiana Senate District 29 in 2018, defeating the Republican incumbent; is the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly.

Serves on the Indiana Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees in the 2025-2026 session.

priorities.text: Names affordability as a top message, saying he would work to block what he describes as anti-competitive hospital, insurance, and grocery mergers.
priorities.quote: We have a monopoly problem, and I'm going to tackle it by restoring competition to the market. I'll work to block anti-competitive hospital and insurance mergers, block grocery mega-mergers that kill local choice, and ensure our utility bills don't skyrocket just to subsidize energy-hungry data centers for massive corporations.

priorities.text: Names care costs (childcare and senior care) as a priority, calling for an expanded child and dependent care tax credit and national minimum staffing standards for nursing homes.
Says he would maintain an open-door policy with regular town halls, as he did in the Statehouse.

positions.summary: Says he would work to lower healthcare premiums by stopping what he describes as anti-competitive hospital mergers.
Says he would expand the child and dependent care tax credit and treat childcare as essential infrastructure.

record.text: Elected to the Indiana Senate in 2018, flipping the previously Republican-held District 29.

Serves on the Indiana Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees during the 2025-2026 session.
